# PRACTICE DIRECTION 56 – LANDLORD AND TENANT CLAIMS AND MISCELLANEOUS PROVISIONS ABOUT LAND

# This Practice Direction supplements Part 56

[This Practice Direction supplements Part 56] Contents of this Practice Direction

## SECTION I – LANDLORD AND TENANT CLAIMS

## 1.1 In this section of this practice direction –

[This Practice Direction supplements Part 56 > 1.1 In this section of this practice direction –] (1) ‘the 1927 Act’ means the Landlord and Tenant Act 1927;

[This Practice Direction supplements Part 56 > 1.1 In this section of this practice direction –] (2) ‘the 1954 Act’ means the Landlord and Tenant Act 1954;

[This Practice Direction supplements Part 56 > 1.1 In this section of this practice direction –] (3) ‘the 1985 Act’ means the Landlord and Tenant Act 1985; and

[This Practice Direction supplements Part 56 > 1.1 In this section of this practice direction –] (4) ‘the 1987 Act’ means the Landlord and Tenant Act 1987. ## 56.2 – STARTING THE CLAIM

[This Practice Direction supplements Part 56 > 56.2 – STARTING THE CLAIM] 2.1 Subject to paragraph 2.1A, the claimant in a landlord and tenant claim must use the Part 8 procedure as modified by Part 56 and this practice direction. ## 2.1A Where the landlord and tenant claim is a claim for –

[This Practice Direction supplements Part 56 > 2.1A Where the landlord and tenant claim is a claim for –] (1) a new tenancy under section 24 of the 1954 Act in circumstances where the grant of a new tenancy is opposed; or

[This Practice Direction supplements Part 56 > 2.1A Where the landlord and tenant claim is a claim for –] (2) the termination of a tenancy under section 29(2) of the 1954 Act,

[This Practice Direction supplements Part 56 > 2.1A Where the landlord and tenant claim is a claim for –] the claimant must use the Part 7 procedure as modified by Part 56 and this practice direction. ## 2.2

[This Practice Direction supplements Part 56 > 2.2] (1) Except where the county court does not have jurisdiction , landlord and tenant claims should normally be brought in the county court. Only exceptional circumstances justify starting a claim in the High Court. [This Practice Direction supplements Part 56 > 2.2] (2) In the County Court, the claim will be issued by the County Court hearing centre where the claim is made and will then be sent to the County Court hearing centre which serves the address where the land is situated. A claimant should consider the potential delay which may result if a claim is not sent to the appropriate County Court hearing centre in the first instance. [This Practice Direction supplements Part 56 > 2.2] 2.3 If a claimant starts a claim in the High Court and the court decides that it should have been started in the county court, the court will normally either strike the claim out or transfer it to the county court on its own initiative. This is likely to result in delay and the court will normally disallow the costs of starting the claim in the High Court and of any transfer. [This Practice Direction supplements Part 56 > 2.2] 2.4 Circumstances which may, in an appropriate case, justify starting a claim in the High Court are if –

[This Practice Direction supplements Part 56 > 2.2] (1) there are complicated disputes of fact; or

[This Practice Direction supplements Part 56 > 2.2] (2) there are points of law of general importance. [This Practice Direction supplements Part 56 > 2.2] 2.5 The value of the property and the amount of any financial claim may be relevant circumstances, but these factors alone will not normally justify starting the claim in the High Court. ## 2.6 A landlord and tenant claim started in the High Court must be brought in the Chancery Division. [This Practice Direction supplements Part 56 > 2.6 A landlord and tenant claim started in the High Court must be brought in the Chancery Division.] (Where the tenant is a tied pub tenant of a pub-owning business under the Small Business Enterprise and Employment Act 2015, the procedure provided by paragraphs 3.1 to 3.19 of this practice direction is modified by paragraphs 3.20 to 3.32.)

[This Practice Direction supplements Part 56 > 2.6 A landlord and tenant claim started in the High Court must be brought in the Chancery Division.] 3.1 This paragraph applies to a claim for a new tenancy under section 24 and termination of a tenancy under section 29(2) of the 1954 Act where rule 56.3 applies and in this paragraph –

[This Practice Direction supplements Part 56 > 2.6 A landlord and tenant claim started in the High Court must be brought in the Chancery Division.] (1) ‘an unopposed claim’ means a claim for a new tenancy under section 24 of the 1954 Act in circumstances where the grant of a new tenancy is not opposed;

[This Practice Direction supplements Part 56 > 2.6 A landlord and tenant claim started in the High Court must be brought in the Chancery Division.] (2) ‘an opposed claim’ means a claim for –

[This Practice Direction supplements Part 56 > 2.6 A landlord and tenant claim started in the High Court must be brought in the Chancery Division.] (a) a new tenancy under section 24 of the 1954 Act in circumstances where the grant of a new tenancy is opposed; or

[This Practice Direction supplements Part 56 > 2.6 A landlord and tenant claim started in the High Court must be brought in the Chancery Division.] (b) the termination of a tenancy under section 29(2) of the 1954 Act; and

[This Practice Direction supplements Part 56 > 2.6 A landlord and tenant claim started in the High Court must be brought in the Chancery Division.] (3) ‘grounds of opposition’ means –

[This Practice Direction supplements Part 56 > 2.6 A landlord and tenant claim started in the High Court must be brought in the Chancery Division.] (a) the grounds specified in section 30(1) of the 1954 Act on which a landlord may oppose an application for a new tenancy under section 24(1) of the 1954 Act or make an application under section 29(2) of the 1954 Act; or

[This Practice Direction supplements Part 56 > 2.6 A landlord and tenant claim started in the High Court must be brought in the Chancery Division.] (b) any other basis on which the landlord asserts that a new tenancy ought not to be granted. [This Practice Direction supplements Part 56 > 2.6 A landlord and tenant claim started in the High Court must be brought in the Chancery Division.] 3.2 Where more than one application to the court under section 24(1) or section 29(2) of the 1954 Act is made, the following provisions shall apply –

[This Practice Direction supplements Part 56 > 2.6 A landlord and tenant claim started in the High Court must be brought in the Chancery Division.] (1) once an application to the court under section 24(1) of the 1954 Act has been served on a defendant, no further application to the court in respect of the same tenancy whether under section 24(1) or section 29(2) of the 1954 Act may be served by that defendant without the permission of the court;

[This Practice Direction supplements Part 56 > 2.6 A landlord and tenant claim started in the High Court must be brought in the Chancery Division.] (2) if more than one application to the court under section 24(1) of the 1954 Act in respect of the same tenancy is served on the same day, any landlord’s application shall stand stayed until further order of the court;

[This Practice Direction supplements Part 56 > 2.6 A landlord and tenant claim started in the High Court must be brought in the Chancery Division.] (3) if applications to the court under both section 24(1) and section 29(2) of the 1954 Act in respect of the same tenancy are served on the same day, any tenant’s application shall stand stayed until further order of the court; and

[This Practice Direction supplements Part 56 > 2.6 A landlord and tenant claim started in the High Court must be brought in the Chancery Division.] (4) if a defendant is served with an application under section 29(2) of the 1954 Act (‘the section 29(2) application’) which was issued at a time when an application to the court had already been made by that defendant in respect of the same tenancy under section 24(1) of the 1954 Act (‘the section 24(1) application’), the service of the section 29(2) application shall be deemed to be a notice under rule 7.7 requiring service or discontinuance of the section 24(1) application within a period of 14 days after the service of the section 29(2) application. [This Practice Direction supplements Part 56 > 2.6 A landlord and tenant claim started in the High Court must be brought in the Chancery Division.] 3.3 Where a claim for a new tenancy under section 24 of the 1954 Act is made by a tenant, the person who, in relation to the claimant’s current tenancy, is the landlord as defined in section 44 of the 1954 Act must be a defendant. ## Contents of the claim form in all cases

## 3.4 The claim form must contain details of –

[This Practice Direction supplements Part 56 > 3.4 The claim form must contain details of –] (1) the property to which the claim relates;

[This Practice Direction supplements Part 56 > 3.4 The claim form must contain details of –] (2) the particulars of the current tenancy (including date, parties and duration), the current rent (if not the original rent) and the date and method of termination;

[This Practice Direction supplements Part 56 > 3.4 The claim form must contain details of –] (3) every notice or request given or made under sections 25 or 26 of the 1954 Act; and

[This Practice Direction supplements Part 56 > 3.4 The claim form must contain details of –] (4) the expiry date of –

[This Practice Direction supplements Part 56 > 3.4 The claim form must contain details of –] (a) the statutory period under section 29A(2) of the 1954 Act; or

[This Practice Direction supplements Part 56 > 3.4 The claim form must contain details of –] (b) any agreed extended period made under section 29B(1) or 29B(2) of the 1954 Act. [This Practice Direction supplements Part 56 > 3.4 The claim form must contain details of –] 3.5 Where the claimant is the tenant making a claim for a new tenancy under section 24 of the 1954 Act, in addition to the details specified in paragraph 3.4, the claim form must contain details of –

[This Practice Direction supplements Part 56 > 3.4 The claim form must contain details of –] (1) the nature of the business carried on at the property;

[This Practice Direction supplements Part 56 > 3.4 The claim form must contain details of –] (2) whether the claimant relies on section 23(1A), 41 or 42 of the 1954 Act and, if so, the basis on which he does so;

[This Practice Direction supplements Part 56 > 3.4 The claim form must contain details of –] (3) whether the claimant relies on section 31A of the 1954 Act and, if so, the basis on which he does so;

[This Practice Direction supplements Part 56 > 3.4 The claim form must contain details of –] (4) whether any, and if so what part, of the property comprised in the tenancy is occupied neither by the claimant nor by a person employed by the claimant for the purpose of the claimant’s business;

[This Practice Direction supplements Part 56 > 3.4 The claim form must contain details of –] (5) the claimant’s proposed terms of the new tenancy; and

[This Practice Direction supplements Part 56 > 3.4 The claim form must contain details of –] (6) the name and address of –

[This Practice Direction supplements Part 56 > 3.4 The claim form must contain details of –] (a) anyone known to the claimant who has an interest in the reversion in the property (whether immediate or in not more than 15 years) on the termination of the claimant’s current tenancy and who is likely to be affected by the grant of a new tenancy; or

[This Practice Direction supplements Part 56 > 3.4 The claim form must contain details of –] (b) if the claimant does not know of anyone specified by sub-paragraph (6)(a), anyone who has a freehold interest in the property. [This Practice Direction supplements Part 56 > 3.4 The claim form must contain details of –] 3.6 The claim form must be served on the persons referred to in paragraph 3.5(6)(a) or (b) as appropriate. [This Practice Direction supplements Part 56 > 3.4 The claim form must contain details of –] 3.7 Where the claimant is the landlord making a claim for a new tenancy under section 24 of the 1954 Act, in addition to the details specified in paragraph 3.4, the claim form must contain details of –

[This Practice Direction supplements Part 56 > 3.4 The claim form must contain details of –] (1) the claimant’s proposed terms of the new tenancy;

[This Practice Direction supplements Part 56 > 3.4 The claim form must contain details of –] (2) whether the claimant is aware that the defendant’s tenancy is one to which section 32(2) of the 1954 Act applies and, if so, whether the claimant requires that any new tenancy shall be a tenancy of the whole of the property comprised in the defendant’s current tenancy or just of the holding as defined by section 23(3) of the 1954 Act; and

[This Practice Direction supplements Part 56 > 3.4 The claim form must contain details of –] (3) the name and address of –

[This Practice Direction supplements Part 56 > 3.4 The claim form must contain details of –] (a) anyone known to the claimant who has an interest in the reversion in the property (whether immediate or in not more than 15 years) on the termination of the claimant’s current tenancy and who is likely to be affected by the grant of a new tenancy; or

[This Practice Direction supplements Part 56 > 3.4 The claim form must contain details of –] (b) if the claimant does not know of anyone specified by sub-paragraph (3)(a), anyone who has a freehold interest in the property. [This Practice Direction supplements Part 56 > 3.4 The claim form must contain details of –] 3.8 The claim form must be served on the persons referred to in paragraph 3.7(3)(a) or (b) as appropriate. [This Practice Direction supplements Part 56 > 3.4 The claim form must contain details of –] 3.9 Where the claimant is the landlord making an application for the termination of a tenancy under section 29(2) of the 1954 Act, in addition to the details specified in paragraph 3.4, the claim form must contain –

[This Practice Direction supplements Part 56 > 3.4 The claim form must contain details of –] (1) the claimant’s grounds of opposition;

[This Practice Direction supplements Part 56 > 3.4 The claim form must contain details of –] (2) full details of those grounds of opposition; and

[This Practice Direction supplements Part 56 > 3.4 The claim form must contain details of –] (3) the terms of a new tenancy that the claimant proposes in the event that his claim fails. [This Practice Direction supplements Part 56 > 3.4 The claim form must contain details of –] 3.10 Where the claim is an unopposed claim and the claimant is the tenant, the acknowledgment of service is to be in form N210 and must state with particulars –

[This Practice Direction supplements Part 56 > 3.4 The claim form must contain details of –] (1) whether, if a new tenancy is granted, the defendant objects to any of the terms proposed by the claimant and if so –

[This Practice Direction supplements Part 56 > 3.4 The claim form must contain details of –] (a) the terms to which he objects; and

[This Practice Direction supplements Part 56 > 3.4 The claim form must contain details of –] (a) the terms that he proposes in so far as they differ from those proposed by the claimant;

[This Practice Direction supplements Part 56 > 3.4 The claim form must contain details of –] (2) whether the defendant is a tenant under a lease having less than 15 years unexpired at the date of the termination of the claimant’s current tenancy and, if so, the name and address of any person who, to the knowledge of the defendant, has an interest in the reversion in the property expectant (whether immediate or in not more than 15 years from that date) on the termination of the defendant’s tenancy;

[This Practice Direction supplements Part 56 > 3.4 The claim form must contain details of –] (3) the name and address of any person having an interest in the property who is likely to be affected by the grant of a new tenancy; and

[This Practice Direction supplements Part 56 > 3.4 The claim form must contain details of –] (4) if the claimant’s current tenancy is one to which section 32(2) of the 1954 Act applies, whether the defendant requires that any new tenancy shall be a tenancy of the whole of the property comprised in the claimant’s current tenancy. ## Acknowledgment of service where the claim is an unopposed claim and the claimant is the landlord

[This Practice Direction supplements Part 56 > Acknowledgment of service where the claim is an unopposed claim and the claimant is the landlord] 3.11 Where the claim is an unopposed claim and the claimant is the landlord, the acknowledgment of service is to be in form N210 and must state with particulars –

[This Practice Direction supplements Part 56 > Acknowledgment of service where the claim is an unopposed claim and the claimant is the landlord] (1) the nature of the business carried on at the property;

[This Practice Direction supplements Part 56 > Acknowledgment of service where the claim is an unopposed claim and the claimant is the landlord] (2) if the defendant relies on section 23(1A), 41 or 42 of the 1954 Act, the basis on which he does so;

[This Practice Direction supplements Part 56 > Acknowledgment of service where the claim is an unopposed claim and the claimant is the landlord] (3) whether any, and if so what part, of the property comprised in the tenancy is occupied neither by the defendant nor by a person employed by the defendant for the purpose of the defendant’s business;

[This Practice Direction supplements Part 56 > Acknowledgment of service where the claim is an unopposed claim and the claimant is the landlord] (4) the name and address of –

[This Practice Direction supplements Part 56 > Acknowledgment of service where the claim is an unopposed claim and the claimant is the landlord] (a) anyone known to the defendant who has an interest in the reversion in the property (whether immediate or in not more than 15 years) on the termination of the defendant’s current tenancy and who is likely to be affected by the grant of a new tenancy; or

[This Practice Direction supplements Part 56 > Acknowledgment of service where the claim is an unopposed claim and the claimant is the landlord] (b) if the defendant does not know of anyone specified by sub-paragraph (4)(a), anyone who has a freehold interest in the property; and

[This Practice Direction supplements Part 56 > Acknowledgment of service where the claim is an unopposed claim and the claimant is the landlord] (5) whether, if a new tenancy is granted, the defendant objects to any of the terms proposed by the claimant and, if so –

[This Practice Direction supplements Part 56 > Acknowledgment of service where the claim is an unopposed claim and the claimant is the landlord] (a) the terms to which he objects; and

[This Practice Direction supplements Part 56 > Acknowledgment of service where the claim is an unopposed claim and the claimant is the landlord] (b) the terms that he proposes in so far as they differ from those proposed by the claimant. ## 3.12 Where the claim is an opposed claim and the claimant is the tenant –

[This Practice Direction supplements Part 56 > 3.12 Where the claim is an opposed claim and the claimant is the tenant –] (1) the acknowledgment of service is to be in form N9; and

[This Practice Direction supplements Part 56 > 3.12 Where the claim is an opposed claim and the claimant is the tenant –] (2) in his defence the defendant must state with particulars –

[This Practice Direction supplements Part 56 > 3.12 Where the claim is an opposed claim and the claimant is the tenant –] (a) the defendant’s grounds of opposition;

[This Practice Direction supplements Part 56 > 3.12 Where the claim is an opposed claim and the claimant is the tenant –] (b) full details of those grounds of opposition;

[This Practice Direction supplements Part 56 > 3.12 Where the claim is an opposed claim and the claimant is the tenant –] (c) whether, if a new tenancy is granted, the defendant objects to any of the terms proposed by the claimant and if so –

[This Practice Direction supplements Part 56 > 3.12 Where the claim is an opposed claim and the claimant is the tenant –] (i) the terms to which he objects; and

[This Practice Direction supplements Part 56 > 3.12 Where the claim is an opposed claim and the claimant is the tenant –] (ii) the terms that he proposes in so far as they differ from those proposed by the claimant;

[This Practice Direction supplements Part 56 > 3.12 Where the claim is an opposed claim and the claimant is the tenant –] (d) whether the defendant is a tenant under a lease having less than 15 years unexpired at the date of the termination of the claimant’s current tenancy and, if so, the name and address of any person who, to the knowledge of the defendant, has an interest in the reversion in the property expectant (whether immediately or in not more than 15 years from that date) on the termination of the defendant’s tenancy;

[This Practice Direction supplements Part 56 > 3.12 Where the claim is an opposed claim and the claimant is the tenant –] (e) the name and address of any person having an interest in the property who is likely to be affected by the grant of a new tenancy; and

[This Practice Direction supplements Part 56 > 3.12 Where the claim is an opposed claim and the claimant is the tenant –] (f) if the claimant’s current tenancy is one to which section 32(2) of the 1954 Act applies, whether the defendant requires that any new tenancy shall be a tenancy of the whole of the property comprised in the claimant’s current tenancy. ## 3.13 Where the claim is an opposed claim and the claimant is the landlord –

[This Practice Direction supplements Part 56 > 3.13 Where the claim is an opposed claim and the claimant is the landlord –] (1) the acknowledgment of service is to be in form N9; and

[This Practice Direction supplements Part 56 > 3.13 Where the claim is an opposed claim and the claimant is the landlord –] (2) in his defence the defendant must state with particulars –

[This Practice Direction supplements Part 56 > 3.13 Where the claim is an opposed claim and the claimant is the landlord –] (a) whether the defendant relies on section 23(1A), 41 or 42 of the 1954 Act and, if so, the basis on which he does so;

[This Practice Direction supplements Part 56 > 3.13 Where the claim is an opposed claim and the claimant is the landlord –] (b) whether the defendant relies on section 31A of the 1954 Act and, if so, the basis on which he does so; and

[This Practice Direction supplements Part 56 > 3.13 Where the claim is an opposed claim and the claimant is the landlord –] (c) the terms of the new tenancy that the defendant would propose in the event that the claimant’s claim to terminate the current tenancy fails. ## Evidence in an unopposed claim

[This Practice Direction supplements Part 56 > Evidence in an unopposed claim] 3.14 Where the claim is an unopposed claim, no evidence need be filed unless and until the court directs it to be filed. ## Evidence in an opposed claim

[This Practice Direction supplements Part 56 > Evidence in an opposed claim] 3.15 Where the claim is an opposed claim, evidence (including expert evidence) must be filed by the parties as the court directs and the landlord shall be required to file his evidence first. ## Grounds of opposition to be tried as a preliminary issue

[This Practice Direction supplements Part 56 > Grounds of opposition to be tried as a preliminary issue] 3.16 Unless in the circumstances of the case it is unreasonable to do so, any grounds of opposition shall be tried as a preliminary issue. ## Applications for interim rent under section 24A to 24D of the 1954 Act

[This Practice Direction supplements Part 56 > Applications for interim rent under section 24A to 24D of the 1954 Act] 3.17 Where proceedings have already been commenced for the grant of a new tenancy or the termination of an existing tenancy, the claim for interim rent under section 24A of the 1954 Act shall be made in those proceedings by –

[This Practice Direction supplements Part 56 > Applications for interim rent under section 24A to 24D of the 1954 Act] (1) the claim form;

[This Practice Direction supplements Part 56 > Applications for interim rent under section 24A to 24D of the 1954 Act] (2) the acknowledgment of service or defence; or

[This Practice Direction supplements Part 56 > Applications for interim rent under section 24A to 24D of the 1954 Act] (3) an application on notice under Part 23. [This Practice Direction supplements Part 56 > Applications for interim rent under section 24A to 24D of the 1954 Act] 3.18 Any application under section 24D(3) of the 1954 Act shall be made by an application on notice under Part 23 in the original proceedings. [This Practice Direction supplements Part 56 > Applications for interim rent under section 24A to 24D of the 1954 Act] 3.19 Where no other proceedings have been commenced for the grant of a new tenancy or termination of an existing tenancy or where such proceedings have been disposed of, an application for interim rent under section 24A of the 1954 Act shall be made under the procedure in Part 8 and the claim form shall include details of –

[This Practice Direction supplements Part 56 > Applications for interim rent under section 24A to 24D of the 1954 Act] (1) the property to which the claim relates;

[This Practice Direction supplements Part 56 > Applications for interim rent under section 24A to 24D of the 1954 Act] (2) the particulars of the relevant tenancy (including date, parties and duration) and the current rent (if not the original rent);

[This Practice Direction supplements Part 56 > Applications for interim rent under section 24A to 24D of the 1954 Act] (3) every notice or request given or made under sections 25 or 26 of the 1954 Act;

[This Practice Direction supplements Part 56 > Applications for interim rent under section 24A to 24D of the 1954 Act] (4) if the relevant tenancy has terminated, the date and mode of termination; and

[This Practice Direction supplements Part 56 > Applications for interim rent under section 24A to 24D of the 1954 Act] (5) if the relevant tenancy has been terminated and the landlord has granted a new tenancy of the property to the tenant –

[This Practice Direction supplements Part 56 > Applications for interim rent under section 24A to 24D of the 1954 Act] (a) particulars of the new tenancy (including date, parties and duration) and the rent; and

[This Practice Direction supplements Part 56 > Applications for interim rent under section 24A to 24D of the 1954 Act] (b) in a case where section 24C(2) of the 1954 Act applies but the claimant seeks a different rent under section 24C(3) of that Act, particulars and matters on which the claimant relies as satisfying section 24C(3). ## Pubs Code tenants

## 3.20 In the following paragraphs –

[This Practice Direction supplements Part 56 > 3.20 In the following paragraphs –] (1) ‘end of the MRO procedure’ means the day calculated in accordance with regulation 39(4) of the Pubs Code;

[This Practice Direction supplements Part 56 > 3.20 In the following paragraphs –] (2) ‘MRO’ means market rent only option as provided by section 43 of the Small Business, Enterprise and Employment Act 2015;

[This Practice Direction supplements Part 56 > 3.20 In the following paragraphs –] (3) ‘MRO notice’ has the meaning given in regulation 23(1) of the Pubs Code;

[This Practice Direction supplements Part 56 > 3.20 In the following paragraphs –] (4) ‘MRO tenancy’ is a tenancy to occupy premises on MRO terms and provided in compliance with the Pubs Code;

[This Practice Direction supplements Part 56 > 3.20 In the following paragraphs –] (5) ‘pub-owning business’ has the meaning given in section 69(1) of the Small Business, Enterprise and Employment Act 2015;

[This Practice Direction supplements Part 56 > 3.20 In the following paragraphs –] (6) ‘Pubs Code’, means the Pubs Code Etc. Regulations 2016; (7) ‘Pubs Code Adjudicator’ is the corporation sole body established by section 41 of the Small Business, Enterprise and Employment Act 2015;

[This Practice Direction supplements Part 56 > 3.20 In the following paragraphs –] (8) ‘Pubs Code tenant’ means a tied pub tenant whose immediate landlord is a pub-owning business; and

[This Practice Direction supplements Part 56 > 3.20 In the following paragraphs –] (9) ‘tied pub tenant” has the meaning given in section 70(1) of the Small Business, Enterprise and Employment Act 2015. [This Practice Direction supplements Part 56 > 3.20 In the following paragraphs –] 3.21 Where the tenant is a Pubs Code tenant, paragraphs 1.1 – 3.19 apply, subject to the following modifications. ## Contents of the claim form where a party is a Pubs Code tenant

[This Practice Direction supplements Part 56 > Contents of the claim form where a party is a Pubs Code tenant] 3.22 In addition to the details listed at paragraph 3.4, the claim form must state that the tenant is a Pubs Code tenant. ## 3.23 The claim form must state whether the tenant –

[This Practice Direction supplements Part 56 > 3.23 The claim form must state whether the tenant –] (1) has given an MRO notice in accordance with the Pubs Code;

[This Practice Direction supplements Part 56 > 3.23 The claim form must state whether the tenant –] (2) has requested a rent proposal in accordance with Regulation 15(1)-(5) of the Pubs Code. [This Practice Direction supplements Part 56 > 3.23 The claim form must state whether the tenant –] 3.24 Where the tenant has given an MRO notice or has requested a rent proposal as referred to in paragraph 3.23(1) or (2), the claimant may choose to state the proposed terms of the new tenancy, but is not obliged to do so. ## Acknowledgment of service and defence where a party is a Pubs Code tenant

[This Practice Direction supplements Part 56 > Acknowledgment of service and defence where a party is a Pubs Code tenant] 3.25 Where an MRO notice has been given by the Pubs Code tenant or the claim form does not state proposed terms of the new tenancy, there is no requirement for the defendant to state in the acknowledgement of service or defence the terms of any new tenancy proposed in the claim form to which the defendant objects, or the terms the defendant proposes. ## Unopposed claim where a Pubs Code tenant has given an MRO notice

[This Practice Direction supplements Part 56 > Unopposed claim where a Pubs Code tenant has given an MRO notice] 3.26 In an unopposed claim where a Pubs Code tenant has given an MRO notice, following the filing of the acknowledgement of service, the court must consider whether to stay the claim pending the end of the MRO procedure. [This Practice Direction supplements Part 56 > Unopposed claim where a Pubs Code tenant has given an MRO notice] 3.27 Where the court has stayed proceedings under paragraph 3.26, the claimant must notify the court within 28 days following the end of the MRO procedure –

[This Practice Direction supplements Part 56 > Unopposed claim where a Pubs Code tenant has given an MRO notice] (1) whether any tenancy has been accepted; and

[This Practice Direction supplements Part 56 > Unopposed claim where a Pubs Code tenant has given an MRO notice] (2) where a tenancy has been accepted –

[This Practice Direction supplements Part 56 > Unopposed claim where a Pubs Code tenant has given an MRO notice] (a) the terms of the new tenancy; and

[This Practice Direction supplements Part 56 > Unopposed claim where a Pubs Code tenant has given an MRO notice] (b) whether any part of the claim is left for the court to determine (such as interim rent) and if so, what those matters are; or

[This Practice Direction supplements Part 56 > Unopposed claim where a Pubs Code tenant has given an MRO notice] (3) where no tenancy has been accepted, whether any terms of a proposed tied tenancy have been the subject of determination by the Pubs Code Adjudicator,

[This Practice Direction supplements Part 56 > Unopposed claim where a Pubs Code tenant has given an MRO notice] and in every case must file at the same time a consent order for disposal of the proceedings or proposed directions for the further conduct of the proceedings indicating whether those directions have been agreed with the defendant. ## Grounds of opposition where a party is a Pubs Code tenant who has given an MRO notice

[This Practice Direction supplements Part 56 > Grounds of opposition where a party is a Pubs Code tenant who has given an MRO notice] 3.28 If the court dismisses the grounds of opposition in a claim where a party is a Pubs Code tenant who has given an MRO notice, the court must consider whether to stay the court proceedings pending the end of the MRO procedure.
